\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பணிநீக்கம்} (paṇinīkkam)}{பணிநீக்கம் (paṇinīkkam)}]{\ta{பணிநீக்கம்} (paṇinīkkam) — dismissal; the sack}

\label{lesson:TA-C512-paninikkam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a businessman, then the Tamil for a partner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பணிநீக்கம்}}
\textbf{\ta{பணிநீக்கம்}} — \emph{paṇinīkkam} — \textquotedblleft{}dismissal; the sack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நிறுவனம்} \ta{நஷ்டம்} \ta{அடைந்ததால்} \ta{பலர்} \ta{பணிநீக்கம்} \ta{செய்யப்பட்டார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{niṟuvaṉam naṣṭam aṭaintatāl palar paṇinīkkam ceyyappaṭṭārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because the company made a loss, many people were dismissed.
\end{quote}

\ta{பணி} \textquotedblleft{}work, service\textquotedblright{} + \ta{நீக்கம்} \textquotedblleft{}removal\textquotedblright{}. With \ta{செய்} it is a verb: \ta{பணிநீக்கம்} \ta{செய்}, to dismiss.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பணிநீக்கம்}} (\emph{paṇinīkkam}) is a native compound: \ta{பணி} (\emph{paṇi}), \textquotedblleft{}work, service\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3884), and \ta{நீக்கம்} (\emph{nīkkam}), \textquotedblleft{}removal\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{நீக்கு}, \textquotedblleft{}to remove\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3685).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇinīkkam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇinīkkam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niṟuvaṉam naṣṭam aṭaintatāl palar paṇinīkkam ceyyappaṭṭārkaḷ.} — Because the company made a loss, many people were dismissed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a businessman, then the Tamil for a partner, then say \emph{paṇinīkkam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகு} (patavi vilaku)}{பதவி விலகு (patavi vilaku)}]{\ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகு} (patavi vilaku) — to resign}

\label{lesson:TA-C512-patavi-vilaku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a partner, then the Tamil for dismissal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகு}}
\textbf{\ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகு}} — \emph{patavi vilaku} — \textquotedblleft{}to resign\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{உடல்நலம்} \ta{சரியில்லாததால்} \ta{தலைவர்} \ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகினார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{uṭalnalam cariyillātatāl talaivar patavi vilakiṉār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The president resigned because of poor health.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகினேன்}, \emph{patavi vilakiṉēṉ}.

Word for word \textquotedblleft{}to step away from a post\textquotedblright{}. \ta{விலகு} alone means \textquotedblleft{}to move aside\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பதவி} \ta{விலகு}} (\emph{patavi vilaku}) joins \ta{பதவி} (\emph{patavi}), \textquotedblleft{}a post\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{padavī} (Monier-Williams), and the native verb \ta{விலகு} (\emph{vilaku}), \textquotedblleft{}to move away, to step aside\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patavi vilaku}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patavi vilaku}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṭalnalam cariyillātatāl talaivar patavi vilakiṉār.} — The president resigned because of poor health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a partner, then the Tamil for dismissal, then say \emph{patavi vilaku} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு} (ōyvu peṟu)}{ஓய்வு பெறு (ōyvu peṟu)}]{\ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு} (ōyvu peṟu) — to retire}

\label{lesson:TA-C512-oyvu-peru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for dismissal, then the Tamil for to resign.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு}}
\textbf{\ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு}} — \emph{ōyvu peṟu} — \textquotedblleft{}to retire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{என்} \ta{தாத்தா} \ta{அறுபது} \ta{வயதில்} \ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெற்றார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ tāttā aṟupatu vayatil ōyvu peṟṟār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather retired at sixty.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெற்றேன்}, \emph{ōyvu peṟṟēṉ}.

Not \textquotedblleft{}to get some rest\textquotedblright{}: \ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு} means leaving one's working life. Rest after work is \ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{எடு} (\emph{ōyvu eṭu}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஓய்வு} \ta{பெறு}} (\emph{ōyvu peṟu}) joins \ta{ஓய்வு} (\emph{ōyvu}), \textquotedblleft{}rest\textquotedblright{}, and the native \ta{பெறு} (\emph{peṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}to get, to receive\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4422); together they mean receiving one's rest from working life.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōyvu peṟu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōyvu peṟu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉ tāttā aṟupatu vayatil ōyvu peṟṟār.} — My grandfather retired at sixty.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for dismissal, then the Tamil for to resign, then say \emph{ōyvu peṟu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{இடமாற்றம்} (iṭamāṟṟam)}{இடமாற்றம் (iṭamāṟṟam)}]{\ta{இடமாற்றம்} (iṭamāṟṟam) — a transfer}

\label{lesson:TA-C512-itamarram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to resign, then the Tamil for to retire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இடமாற்றம்}}
\textbf{\ta{இடமாற்றம்}} — \emph{iṭamāṟṟam} — \textquotedblleft{}a transfer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அப்பாவுக்கு} \ta{வேறு} \ta{ஊருக்கு} \ta{இடமாற்றம்} \ta{கிடைத்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{appāvukku vēṟu ūrukku iṭamāṟṟam kiṭaittatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father got a transfer to another town.
\end{quote}

\ta{இடம்} \textquotedblleft{}a place\textquotedblright{} + \ta{மாற்றம்} \textquotedblleft{}a change\textquotedblright{}: a change of posting.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{இடமாற்றம்}} (\emph{iṭamāṟṟam}) is a native compound: \ta{இடம்} (\emph{iṭam}), \textquotedblleft{}a place\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 434), and \ta{மாற்றம்} (\emph{māṟṟam}), \textquotedblleft{}a change\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{மாறு} (\emph{māṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}to change\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4834).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]

\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭamāṟṟam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{appāvukku vēṟu ūrukku iṭamāṟṟam kiṭaittatu.} — Father got a transfer to another town.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to resign, then the Tamil for to retire, then say \emph{iṭamāṟṟam} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தொடங்கு} (toṭaṅku)}{தொடங்கு (toṭaṅku)}]{\ta{தொடங்கு} (toṭaṅku) — to start; to begin}

\label{lesson:TA-C512-totanku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to retire, then the Tamil for a transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தொடங்கு}}
\textbf{\ta{தொடங்கு}} — \emph{toṭaṅku} — \textquotedblleft{}to start; to begin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவள்} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{சிறிய} \ta{உணவகத்தைத்} \ta{தொடங்கினாள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ oru ciṟiya uṇavakattait toṭaṅkiṉāḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She started a small restaurant.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{தொடங்கினேன்}, \emph{toṭaṅkiṉēṉ}.

Both \textquotedblleft{}to start something\textquotedblright{} (-\ta{ஐ}) and \textquotedblleft{}to begin\textquotedblright{} alone: \ta{கூட்டம்} \ta{தொடங்கியது}, the meeting began. A near twin is \ta{ஆரம்பி} (\emph{ārampi}), from Sanskrit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தொடங்கு}} (\emph{toṭaṅku}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3481 gives \ta{தொடங்கு} (\emph{toṭaṅku}), \textquotedblleft{}to begin, to undertake\textquotedblright{}, beside the older \ta{தொடு}, \textquotedblleft{}to begin\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷ oru ciṟiya uṇavakattait toṭaṅkiṉāḷ.} — She started a small restaurant.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to retire, then the Tamil for a transfer, then say \emph{toṭaṅku} again
\end{itemize}
